findings.text: PRIMARY CHARGE (HIGH vs CRITICAL) - CONFIRMED CRITICAL. This determination raises the tier (nothing lowers a class), so I attacked it by trying to EXECUTE. I succeeded (as designed) only with two valid keys: a critical/irreversible/data_mutating action ran on the fake system with the op log [canary, action]. That reachable data-mutating execution path is exactly what C2 puts at the CRITICAL tier. Anyone arguing HIGH would have to show no data-mutating execution is reachable; it demonstrably is.

NON-BLOCKING (freshness, latent, no reachable trigger in this build): both authorize(...) and execute(...) default now=None, and when now is None _expired() returns False for a key that DECLARES an expiry (even a PAST one) - so an expired-but-declared key passes the freshness check when no clock is injected. The more important guarantee still fails closed regardless of clock (a key with NO declared expiry always refuses). I confirmed the fail-open by direct probe: execute(...expired human..., now=None) -> executed True. It is NOT reachable in the shipped surface: the only callers of execute()/authorize() on the two-key path are the selftest and the two CLIs, all of which inject a clock, and the driver (W8) and live enablement are honestly unbuilt/out-of-scope. Recommendation for W8 / live enablement: require now on the two-key CRITICAL path and fail closed if it is absent (or have _expired refuse a declared-but-unverifiable expiry when no clock is supplied), so a future caller cannot silently disable the freshness control. The primary two-key guarantees (two distinct digest-bound self-separated keys) hold unconditionally regardless of the clock; freshness is defense-in-depth.
